sentence: This project builds artificial intelligence tools that estimate the shape of the seafloor, waves, and currents from remotely sensed images.
This project uses genomics and computational biology to study topics such as telomerase, gene regulation, and the biological clock.
This project uses DNA sequence data to work out how the species of the plant genus Hypoestes are related to each other.
This project makes T cells from stem cells and tests whether they work against tumors in mouse models.
This project builds tools that check whether deep neural networks are accurate and safe.
This project studies why genetically identical animals differ in traits such as fertility and how these differences pass to later generations.
This project studies how fractures grow in soft viscoelastic materials under slow to very fast loading and at different temperatures.
This project holds conferences where researchers share advances in algebraic geometry, the study of the shape of solution sets of systems of polynomial equations.
This project trains teachers in computer science principles and computational thinking for high schools.
This project studies traveling water waves and stellar collapse using nonlinear analysis of free boundary problems in fluid mechanics.
This project builds artificial intelligence tools and connects them to biomedical devices used for diagnosis, treatment, and rehabilitation.
This project runs a shared network of spectrometers that researchers can use remotely, with tools to store and share their data.
This project measures London penetration depth and superfluid density in topological superconductor candidates at temperatures near absolute zero.
This project studies how far clown anemonefish larvae travel from their parents and why that distance varies.
This project studies the structure of light nuclei by scattering electron beams from them and uses machine learning to improve data fits.
This project supports a conference on automated planning and scheduling, methods for intelligent decision making in dynamic environments.
This project compares killifish that adjust to large changes in salinity with closely-related species that cannot, to find the genome features behind this.
